My latest on the Houthis and the broader regional order:

Over the past week, Saudi Arabia has come under attack—on two fronts.
First, in Yemen, the Houthis seized the port city of Mocha on September 10 and advanced along the Red Sea coast toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital waterway for Saudi exports. Meanwhile, drones from Iraq struck Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the roughly 750-mile artery carrying oil from the eastern fields toward Red Sea export terminals.

The attacks coincide with the Iraqi government’s September 30 deadlinefor nonstate groups in the country to disarm, and with mounting U.S. and Israeli pressure on the Islamic Republic that arms and sustains them.

They also come amid a much broader campaign against the regional proxy system that Tehran has spent decades building. Since the U.S. war with Iran began on February 28, Operations Epic Fury and Economic Fury have placed the Islamic Republic under severe military and financial strain, while the U.S. Treasury Department has targeted Iranian oil exports, shadow-fleet tankers, financial intermediaries, and foreign procurement networks.

tweets.text:
I've closed good trades early just because I got tired of watching them.

If you've traded perps you know the annoying part.

You open a position, watch your margin, keep an eye on liquidation, and even when the trade goes your way, the leverage you started with doesn’t necessarily stay there.

A leveraged token handles that differently. Instead of managing the perp yourself, you buy a token that gives you leveraged exposure, while the position underneath keeps rebalancing toward the target.

That’s basically what @BounceTech is doing. Its leveraged tokens are ERC-20s backed by Hyperliquid perp positions, so the rebalancing just happens in the background.

And they’re starting their first trading competition today with $20K+ in prizes.

A $100 buy gets you in automatically, with weekly rewards across PnL, ROI, volume, and profitable finishes.

Take $ZEC for example. Over the past month:

• $ZEC: +132.7%
• Equivalent 5x perp: +663.7%
• Bounce ZEC5L: +1,387.4%

Same market, but the path is very different because the leveraged token keeps rebalancing instead of slowly de-levering as the trade moves in your favour.

That can help a lot in a clean trend. Leveraged tokens are built for trending markets, where compounding can allow them to outperform perps

Whereas in choppy markets, perps can be the better vehicle since they don’t experience the same volatility decay.

Ultimately, leveraged tokens and perps each have environments where they work best, it just comes down to choosing the right instrument for your trade.

The protocol itself has also been picking up:
• $57.7M rolling 30D volume, up 468%
• $2.84M open interest, up 80%
• $384M+ total volume

Perps Dexes gave leverage to traders.

Bounce is packaging that leverage into something that’s easier to hold and manage without sitting on the chart the whole time.

Elon Proposes Adversarial Peer Reviews for AI Safety

@elonmusk:

“What I think would be wise to do as soon as possible, if not immediately, would be to have the major AI competitors test each other's models.

So that you would have everyone's security test harness testing everyone else's model.

So, instead of grading your own homework, you would at least have competitors grading your homework, and raising the alarm if they see concerns.

If competitors say that this model is unsafe, and that model then subsequently does something bad, I think it would be extremely hard to live down. The egg on face level would be very, very high. And the legal liability would be enormous.

And any given proposal has to be something that China is willing to accept, otherwise we're just handicapping ourselves.”

@Jason:

“And Elon, there's no reason these safety and security harnesses and this testing apparatus couldn't be open source, and people could actually supply it. And you'd be able to see under the hood.”

@Chamath

“It creates an incredible incentive for the labs to actually invest in safety because you protect yourself while trying to debunk other people's claims.”

@DavidSacks:

“Well, the product liability point is really key.

Lina Khan actually had a good post, I think it was yesterday, saying that it's not true that we don't have rules and regulations for AI, actually, we do. Product liability laws apply.

And what you're saying, Elon, is that if the companies are doing this test, the peer review, and then one of the companies ignores the feedback and releases it…”

Elon:

“The liability in that case would be enormous.”

Sacks:

“Yes. It would be almost like prima facie evidence that they had been negligent.”

Elon:

“It wouldn't look good to the jury.”

Chamath:

“I like this solution a lot. I like this more than the transnational gulag organization approach.”

Sacks:

“Well, we can do it in a few weeks without some grandiose international... like, we don't need to convene the United Nations to make this happen.”

Chamath:

“No, it's just a decision. It could happen right now.”

Elon:

“You can always escalate the amount of regulatory oversight, but it is very difficult to reduce it.”

Mkt Thoughts - 15 Sept 2026

- First, highly suggest reading QT degentrading's mkt thoughts - has quite good color. Now for my thoughts: 

- On Macro - inflation likely isn't going going back to 2%; Financial conditions haven't tightened at all since May, so the Fed is behind and the job gets harder, not easier.

- On positioning: Exhaustion signals across the whole energy complex; Equities range-bound, funds just deleveraged hard, and nobody has conviction on stocks. 

- And so - actionables: Don't force it, let the market come to you. Have set bids for equities, and decided on clear thematic narratives I want to buy for 6m - 1Y time horizon. Otherwise, this is not a game I'm playing

- Instead, I think crypto offers far more short term upside and is where the hot ball of money is at. It offers better r/r atm - and despite only being 2 weeks, attention feels like its draining away - yet prices are still held up

CLARITY is a nothingburger - obviously positive headline pumped prices but as you can see, it was quickly sold off bc rates aren't actually increasing; I'd like to point out that the entire pump wasn't CLARITY driven in the first place so this macro fud that will come from a lack of approval will probably be good to bid

RH chain continues to be the place to bid long term positions. That, and major alts - looking at VVV and LIT as fastest horses. Overall setting bids on crypto.

Batching, gasless and delegation (moreso than automation) are obvious use cases going back longer than that. It’s why we had a startup centered around it in 2020. 

A very complicated upgrade to consensus isn’t worth that though. There are simpler ways to do that. Especially for gasless and batching which are possible today. (In fact, delegation is also possible today?). The issue is lack of HW support. 

Delegation has an extra problem of verifying what rights you are granted to others (have you tried using a vault product like KPK and checking the zodiac module permissions? The UX is awful). 

Auth, I think is controversial. Not only because HW etc needs to implement it, but implementing verification algorithms for cryptographic protocols in Solidity is slow and error prone. That’s why BTCers have spent years on a super fast ecdsa / schnorr implementation.

Aka this is why I think 8130 is a mistake at consensus. It doesnt matter if a solution ticks all the boxes if it is crazy complicated and over engineered. That technical debt on nodes will be painful and probably lead to loss of user funds.

Such a great story about the impact on communities of a data center created 20 years ago! Re-Industrialization means job creation, new public infrastructure, and thriving small towns! 

« In a time when many rural towns across the country are shrinking, Quincy has grown more than 40 percent, outpacing Seattle. Poverty rates have been cut in half. Over the past two decades, property tax revenue in Grant County has grown twelve-fold, while the rate residents pay has fallen by a third. That revenue has built a new high school, hospital, library and city hall, and it will pay for a future aquatics center.
And at a time when people worry that datacenters bring nothing but a wave of temporary construction jobs, Quincy tells a different story. We've sustained 1,200 construction jobs every year for 20 years by building new datacenters and refurbishing existing ones. We employ close to 700 people on our datacenter campuses in non-construction operational roles. «
